newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, banks favoured.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, banks favoured.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Tuesday with the index sliding while the broader market found some support from selective institutional demand, dealers said.
Funds were seen returning to foreign tranches of banks and blue chips although activity was generally subdued.
"(Activity) got much better in the afternoon on banks," a dealer with a U.S. securities house said, adding sentiment was more positive toward the Singapore budget, due to be announced next week.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed 6.67 points lower at 1,981.28.
Volume was a weak 84 million shares with losers outpacing gainers 194 to 93.
Dealers said the downgrading of regional stocks by analysts had crimped activity recently, but banks were still considered promising despite their large exposure to property loans.
The foreign tranches of DBS rose Singapore 40 cents to S$18.40, and UOB firmed 20 cents to S$14.90.
China-linked stocks which rose sharply ahead of Hong Kong's handover to China eased on Tuesday from profit taking.
Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical was at US$1.10, down five cents. China North Industrial eased to US$0.57, down three cents.
